subject: Biology
title: The Kingdom of Fungi
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Kingdom of Fungi usable.

hook.text: Fungi are not plants. They don't photosynthesize. They digest food externally and absorb it.

buildup.text: The mushroom you see is just the fruiting body. The real organism is a network of threads underground.

discovery.text: Fungi are closer to animals than plants on the tree of life. They share a common ancestor.

twist.text: The largest organism on Earth is a honey fungus in Oregon spanning 2,385 acres.

climax.text: Fungi decompose dead matter, recycle nutrients, and keep forests alive from below the soil.

punchline.text: Mushrooms are just the tip. The real fungus hides below.

quiz.question: Are fungi more closely related to plants or animals?

details.summary: Fungi are a kingdom of eukaryotic organisms that obtain nutrients by decomposing organic matter or parasitizing living hosts. They include mushrooms, yeasts, molds, and lichens. With an estimated 2 to 4 million species, most remain undiscovered in forests and soils worldwide.
details.whyItMatters: Fungi decompose dead matter recycling nutrients essential for all ecosystems. They make bread, beer, cheese, and life-saving drugs like penicillin and cyclosporine possible. Fungi are closer relatives to animals than to plants.
takeaways: Fungi are more closely related to animals than to plants genetically
An estimated 2 to 4 million fungal species exist with most undiscovered
Fungi decompose organic matter recycling essential nutrients in all ecosystems

faq.question: Why are fungi classified separately from plants?
faq.answer: Fungi cannot photosynthesize and obtain nutrients by absorbing dissolved organic matter externally. They have chitin-based cell walls instead of cellulose. Molecular evidence shows fungi share a more recent common ancestor with animals than with plants.

faq.question: What critical roles do fungi play in ecosystems?
faq.answer: Fungi are the primary decomposers of tough plant material like wood and leaf litter. Mycorrhizal fungi help 90 percent of plants absorb nutrients. Lichens colonize bare rock starting soil formation. Without fungal decomposition, dead matter would accumulate indefinitely.
